steps.text: Place tomatoes, tomato paste, parsley, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a food processor; blend until smooth.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook until slightly softened, about 2 minutes.
Stir in blended tomato sauce and white wine.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Marinara Sauce Yet
raw_recipe.description: This marinara sauce recipe is a delicious blend of tomatoes, parsley, garlic, and oregano simmered with onion and white wine for amazing flavor.
raw_recipe.name: Best Marinara Sauce Yet

Stir in blended tomato sauce and white wine.

review.reviewBody: I'm rating this a 5 because the consistency is perfect; thick enough but not too much so that if one wanted to make a meatsauce out of it, the spoon would not stand up straight in the middle of the pot. Also a 5 star for ease of preparation and ingredients one tends to have on hand. I did have to add 2 more cloves of garlic but I am a garlic lover. 1 clove just did not seem to do it justice. I followed exactly and used a 'Mier's Winecellar white table wine'. I added the 1/2 cup and it was not overpowering. I love to cook w/wines but don't drink it and although I could taste it, it wasn't overpowering. It seemed to enhance the flavor and didn't hinder it. It also is a sweeter sort of wine so thought it would help with that sauce tartness thing we all try to fix. I did have to add 1 Tbsp. of BROWN sugar and that took care of it. **I recently saw on Food Network that if you use BROWN sugar in any redsauce, it helps with that tartness fix better than white.** Thanks for the great recipe. I'm going to let it sit in fridge overnight and make eggplant parm. tomorrow.

I substituted chicken broth for the white wine. It was quick, easy and very good the first day. But absolutely wonderful if the ingredients get a chance to "marry" in the fridge for a few days. I'm going to make this in bulk, let it "age" then freeze it so I always have some on hand. Delicious!

I usually buy a certain brand of marinara sauce and then freeze it, but I wanted to see if I was getting my money's worth. And now I know that I wasn't! I followed recipe exactly except I added a clove of garlic, a good handful of Italian seasoning, 2 onions that I *accidentally* cooked to almost caramelized. I'll never buy it again!
**On a second note, I've now used the frozen batch, and it freezes great! Now it's five stars.
**On a third note, if you don't know what to do with the leftover wine and you don't drink it, you can freeze it in ice cube trays for the next time you make this.
**My favorite wine with this so far is a Canadian Riesling. I do NOT like it with red, it has a funny flavor.
GREAT SAUCE. If you try no other try this one. Added fresh basil as well as a bit of sugar to counter the acidity of the tomatoes. Simmering too long degrades the flavor.

Very nice sauce.
Some tips: For those who enjoy garlic, use 1 1/2 to 2 cloves. I used 3 and that was a bit much!
I added 1/4 tsp of medium-heat red pepper flakes for some heat. Yummy! Use 1/3 less oil. If you cook this in a large sauce pan, skillet or fryer, you'll only need to cook it for 15 minutes, not 30. I added a little extra seasoning - as the other reviewers recommended. I also added 1/2 can of tomato sauce because I wanted more sauce for dipping garlic bread into and for the 1/2 pound of meatballs I made.
Refridgerates/reheats very well. Will make again.

People, believe me when I tell you...brown the tomato paste first in a little oil. Medium/low heat. Don't walk away. Just take the redness out, almost brick red. It is a game changer. Anything after that is up to you. Any brand, they are all just tomatoes with the water removed.

I love this marinara sauce! Much better than store bought and, IMHO, better than most Italian restaurants. I recommend doubling the recipe if you are going to make lasagne or another casserole-type dish. I would not double the olive oil, however. And a half cup of white wine is sufficient. Instead of having to wash a food processor, I sauté the onions and then add all remaining ingredients in with the onions. I put a hand-held immersion appliance directly in the pan and gently stir and swirl. Very easy.

Delicious!! First time making it. Read previous comments and added 1 tsp organo , sautéed 2nd garlic clove with the onion and added a shake of crushed red pepper. I did add the pinch of sugar also. My Husband said “best meal you have made in a while”. Served with thin spaghetti and chicken Parmesan. Loved it!
Hands down my absolute red-sauce-go-to! Definitely brown the tomato paste in olive oil first! It adds an incredible flavor! Made this for chicken parm! OUTSTANDING!

Been using this for ages, only change being I do a 50/50 salt/msg for most sauces I make including this one. It’s always a go-to for everything from lasagna to soup base, if I don’t have a spare in the freezer it’s cuz I used the last one left! Today I took it to a whole other level by using a 28oz can of peeled San Marzano tomatoes with 1 oz of the tomato water rinse from the can to equal the 2 cans otherwise. Also added Sauvignon Blanc to the tomato mix pre-blend for better consistency. OMG, so smooth and it absorbs the olive oil beautifully!

I’m not a fan of store bought sauces and this is the first and only sauce I’ve ever made (multiple times). It’s delicious! I cut the oil in half, double the garlic, and eyeball fresh Italian parsley. Then I cook in a slow cooker for 4 hours. I make a double batch since I’m going to the trouble of making homemade sauce and never regret it.

I was extremely dubious of the stewed tomato's. Extremely. They generally include green peppers which in my opinion shouldn’t even be in the room with a good marinara, but I decided, as there were so many five star ratings to just try the recipe as is. I don’t know what sort of witchcraft is involved but this is simply delicious. Somewhere between assembling it and cooking some sort of alchemy is involved. Full disclosure, even though it was pretty amazing prior, I did give it a heaping spoonful of sugar, a glug of good balsamic, and a splash of fish sauce…. But really. *chefs kiss*
Tastes like storebought next time I would replace parsley with basil

My daughter doesn’t like my spaghetti sauce because too much meat and vegetables in it. She says it’s a texture thing. I thought I would try this. I didn’t have any white wine so I used chicken broth. I also added some crushed red pepper. It turned out so good. My daughter loved it! Next time will make enough to freeze
Delicious!!! Easy, simple, and tastes amazing!!

I always used store-bought marinara sauce, but saw this recipe and decided to try it out because I had all the ingredients. It was so easy and after it thickened it tasted even better. I put the brown sugar in as was suggested by others and after browning my meatball, I added them as the sauce was simmering. Absolutely my go-to sauce from now on!
Simple and tastes amazing!
It is a good base to add tour favorite flavors to.
This was excellent and full of flavor! So easy and so good. I used for meatball subs and definitely will make again. Never used a food processor, used my trusty potato masher!

Really easy and good. I made the whole thing in one weeknight pan by heating the oil, add onion, cook till softened, add half garlic, cook 30 seconds, add tomato paste brown slightly. Add wine cook a little. Add tomatoes, spices and balance of garlic. Blend with immersion blender. Simmer covered about 20-30 minutes until thickened. Munge.
